sources.note: the table formerly 'Alternate Titles': lay titles by O*NET-SOC code; 4,504,432 bytes by HEAD on 2026-10-21.  LOAD-BEARING from the first candidate: this generator puts O*NET occupation titles, job titles and lay roles derived from them into candidates.jsonl, the registry, seed-queue entries and readouts by design, so the attribution travels with every run (ATTRIBUTION.md, run.json, each promoted entry's source).  The base-model generator's note said when this would happen: licence verified 2026-10-10 at https://www.onetcenter.org/license_db.html (plan 03 said public domain). Titles are used only as prompt words and no occupation title reaches a tracked artefact, so this attribution is a courtesy, not something we rely on. It becomes LOAD-BEARING the moment a title does reach a tracked artefact - an occupation word surviving as a candidate label in candidate_table*.jsonl, candidates.jsonl, the registry or a readout - and then the attribution above must travel with that artefact (Roger, QUESTIONS 60, 2026-10-11)
